description: Live read-only querying for the dv-query skill against a real Dataverse org. Tests target out-of-box system tables that exist and are non-empty in EVERY org (systemuser always has >=1 enabled user; businessunit always has exactly one root unit), so live runs are deterministic without seeding data. Runs in both simulated (dry-run) and live modes; live-only assertions are stripped in simulated mode via simulated_overrides.
defaultAssertions: PRIORITY_2: FIRST_ATTEMPT: Agent achieved the goal on its first approach without fumbling, error-recovery pivots, or retries that indicate the skill should have guided better

tests.prompt: How many enabled users are in my Dataverse environment? Query the systemuser table and give me the exact count.
tests.expected_response: A read count on the out-of-box systemuser table => dv-query routing: use the SQL (TDS) endpoint (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM systemuser WHERE isdisabled = 0) or an OData $count / aggregate, or MCP query for a single scalar. Report the exact integer count (always >=1 because the environment always has at least one enabled user). Raw urllib/requests is NOT acceptable.
tests.description: Simple scalar count on an always-present out-of-box table (systemuser). Deterministic in any org (>=1 enabled user). Verified live by returning a concrete integer.
assertions: PRIORITY_1: Agent queries the systemuser table using a supported dv-query method — the SQL/TDS endpoint (e.g. SELECT COUNT(*) FROM systemuser), an OData $count/aggregate, or the MCP query tool. A hand-rolled urllib/requests call is NOT acceptable.
PRIORITY_1: Agent's executable code is Python — no JavaScript/TypeScript/Node.js or PowerShell.
PRIORITY_1: Agent actually executed the query against the live org and reported a concrete integer count of enabled users (>=1).

remove_assertions: PRIORITY_1: Agent actually executed the query against the live org and reported a concrete integer count of enabled users (>=1).
add_assertions: PRIORITY_2: Agent states the query it would run and how it would report the count even though it does not execute in dry-run mode.

tests.prompt: What is the name of the root business unit in my Dataverse environment? The root business unit is the one with no parent. Return just its name.
tests.expected_response: A filtered read on the out-of-box businessunit table => dv-query: SQL (SELECT name FROM businessunit WHERE parentbusinessunitid IS NULL) or OData ($filter=parentbusinessunitid eq null, $select=name), or MCP query. Every org has exactly one root business unit, so the result is a single deterministic name. Report just that name. Raw urllib/requests is NOT acceptable.
tests.description: Filtered single-row read on an always-present out-of-box table (businessunit, exactly one root). Deterministic in any org. Verified live by returning the root BU name.

custom_metadata.trap: not filtering for the null-parent root

assertions: PRIORITY_1: Agent queries the businessunit table filtering for the root (parentbusinessunitid IS NULL / eq null) using a supported dv-query method (SQL/TDS, OData $filter, or MCP query) — not raw urllib/requests.
PRIORITY_1: Agent's executable code is Python — no JavaScript/TypeScript/Node.js or PowerShell.
PRIORITY_2: CONTAINS_ANY: parentbusinessunitid, parent business unit, root
PRIORITY_1: Agent actually executed the query against the live org and returned the concrete name of the single root business unit.

remove_assertions: PRIORITY_1: Agent actually executed the query against the live org and returned the concrete name of the single root business unit.
add_assertions: PRIORITY_2: Agent states the filtered query it would run (parentbusinessunitid is null) even though it does not execute in dry-run mode.
